llm.summary: The package contains plausible P2P deployment tooling but also includes unrelated code, embedded credentials, and instructions that cause the agent to read and write sensitive local files and perform remote privileged operations — the footprint is larger and less scoped than the description implies.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to provide P2P messaging and to need SSH + API keys, which fits most of the included deploy/send tooling, but the bundle also contains many unrelated skills and large code trees (openclaw-weibo, imclaw, stock-analysis, etc.). That additional material is not justified by the stated 'Agent P2P' purpose and increases the attack surface.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and included scripts direct the agent to read local OpenClaw config (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, gateway.env), write ~/.openclaw/gateway.env, deploy software over SSH to a VPS, configure systemd/Nginx/Certbot, and start services. AGENTS.md and other docs instruct the agent to automatically read SOUL.md, USER.md and daily memory files — which may contain secrets and private context. This scope goes beyond 'send/receive messages' and allows the agent to access and act on many local secrets and files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no packaged install spec, but included scripts (auto_install.py, deploy scripts) will run shell commands locally and via SSH and clone a GitHub repo on the VPS. The remote install runs apt/certbot/pip and creates systemd units. Executing these scripts implies arbitrary code execution on the user's VPS and local machine; the repo is large and not limited to a single small client binary.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared environment variables (AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN) are plausible for a bridge, but the skill auto-reads local OpenClaw tokens and writes gateway.env without clear user gating. The package itself contains exposed/embedded secrets (e.g., API token in TOOLS.md, passwords and VPS IP stored in MEMORY.md) which are unrelated to a safe install and indicate sensitive data leakage risk. Requesting the OpenClaw hooks token is high-scope because it can wake and interact with the main session.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true, but its scripts persist configuration under ~/.openclaw and can create remote systemd services. Writing its own config is expected; however combined with instructions to auto-read hooks tokens and memory files and to deploy remote services, the privilege to both modify local agent config and operate on a VPS raises a higher blast radius if misused.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Key points to consider before installing:

- This package is much larger than the advertised 'Agent P2P' skill. It includes many unrelated modules and many scripts that will read and write files and execute commands locally and on a remote VPS.
- The auto-install/deploy scripts will: SSH to your VPS, clone code from a GitHub repo, install system packages (nginx, certbot, pip deps), create systemd services, and write configuration under ~/.openclaw. Only proceed if you trust the repo and are prepared to audit the exact commands executed on both machines.
- The repository contains hardcoded/exposed secrets and example credentials (e.g., API keys, a Volces bearer token in TOOLS.md, VPS IPs and passwords in MEMORY.md). Treat those files as evidence the bundle may leak secrets or was crafted from an environment with leftover sensitive data; do not assume they are safe.
- The skill attempts to read your OpenClaw hooks token and gateway config automatically. That token can wake and interact with your main agent session — prefer creating a limited-scope token or avoid giving the hooks token until you review the code.
- Recommended mitigations before use: (1) do a code audit of auto_install.py, deploy scripts, and any server-side code; (2) run installs in an isolated environment or disposable VPS; (3) generate and use a dedicated, restricted SSH key and a dedicated hooks token with minimal permissions; (4) grep the package for 'PRIVATE', 'SECRET', 'TOKEN', 'PASSWORD', and remove any embedded secrets; (5) if you are not comfortable auditing, prefer an official, smaller plugin from a trusted publisher.

If you want, I can: list all files that contain likely secrets, extract lines with 'token', 'password', 'ssh', 'key', and provide the exact commands the auto_install would execute so you can review them before running.
llm.findings: [base64-block] unexpected: The static pre-scan flagged base64-block patterns in SKILL.md content — this can be an attempt to hide payloads or to inject content into evaluation. This is not expected for a simple messaging skill and is suspicious in context.
